result:
I could not finish this problem with confidence, so I can't give a verified numerical answer. Here is the reduction I did establish.

**Reduction.** Let $N = cm$ and let $N'$ be the part of $N$ coprime to 10. Since $\gcd(10^t-1, 10)=1$, the reduced denominator of $\frac{10^t-1}{N}$ has only the primes 2 and 5 exactly when $N' \mid 10^t-1$. This holds exactly when $\operatorname{ord}_{N'}(10) \mid t$. So the $t$ for which the fraction is short are the multiples of $d=\operatorname{ord}_{N'}(10)$, and the minimal such $t$ is $d$ itself. Hence

$$S(m)=\{\operatorname{ord}_{N'}(10) : c\in\{1,\dots,2017\}\},\qquad N' = \text{(10-free part of } cm).$$

**Consequence.** Write $M$ for the 10-free part of $m$. Then $N' = nM$, where $n$ ranges over the integers in $[1,2017]$ coprime to 10 (there are 807 of them). So

$$\max_m |S(m)| = \max_{M \text{ coprime to } 10} \#\{\operatorname{ord}_{nM}(10) : n\le 2017,\ \gcd(n,10)=1\}.$$

For $m=1$, this is the number of distinct multiplicative orders of 10 modulo the $n\le 2017$ coprime to 10. For example, $c=1,7,11$ give $t=1,6,2$. I could not complete the enumeration over all $n$ and over all choices of $M$ by hand, so I cannot determine the maximum. I also have no reliable way to tell whether some $M>1$ does better than $M=1$.

Computing the value requires running the enumeration (for each $M$ candidate, compute $\operatorname{ord}_{nM}(10)$ for all $n\le 2017$ coprime to 10 and count distinct values). I did not run that computation, so I am not giving a numerical answer.

ANSWER: Not determined (the problem reduces to maximizing, over $M$ coprime to 10, the number of distinct values of $\operatorname{ord}_{nM}(10)$ for $n\le 2017$ coprime to 10; I could not complete the computation)
